coverage: Monday pre-Asia-open. US cash shut until tonight; Sunday-evening futures are live. SGX closed for National Day.
tldr: OUR CALL, GRADED — a partial miss. We said crude had over-discounted a Hormuz reopening and to watch the futures open. Oil did gap up, but ~1% not dollars: Brent $84.36 (+1.0%), WTI $78.75 (+0.73%), and roughly half the pop faded within two hours. Right direction, overstated magnitude.

The honest reason: a reopening was never imminent. Tehran published six conditions and Araghchi said there is "no possibility of resuming negotiations" — so there was less mispricing to correct than we implied.

A DATA TRAP nearly made that call look 2.7x better than it was: one source quoted a wrong previous close for Brent, headlining +2.62% instead of ~+1%. Caught before publication; new rule is to verify the reference price before trusting any percent-change field.

ESCALATION IS REAL BUT PRICED AS CONTAINED: tanker strike Saturday, Houthi drone strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery Sunday, Hormuz traffic down ~33% — yet equity futures are flat and GOLD IS LITERALLY UNCHANGED, silver just +0.70% after its 20%+ week.
WEDNESDAY IS THE WEEK: US July CPI and Tencent Q2 results land the same day. Two of your largest exposures resolve together, with September hike odds at ~40-44%.
SGX IS CLOSED TODAY. Tuesday is your only session to position the Singapore sleeve before CPI.
whatChanged: Graded our own Sunday oil call as a partial miss rather than dropping it.
Caught and rejected a bad reference price that would have inflated the apparent move 2.7x, plus futures-vs-cash comparison traps.
Regime: "re-arming oil risk" → "Contained escalation — CPI is the week's only real risk"; risk-on 55% → 57%.
Declared one gap: no Hang Seng futures level could be confirmed.

regime.label: Contained escalation — CPI is the week's only real risk
regime.oneLiner: The Gulf escalated and markets shrugged; Wednesday's CPI, not Hormuz, decides the metals and the September hike.

topNews.headline: OUR CALL, GRADED: oil gapped up — but ~1%, not dollars, and it gave half back within two hours
topNews.actionable: Log this as a partial miss, not a win. For the oil sleeve it is a small positive mark, not a re-rating. The level that matters now: if Brent loses Friday's $83.55 settle during Asian hours, the weekend escalation has been fully round-tripped and the reopening trade reasserts.

topNews.headline: DATA TRAP CAUGHT: a bad reference price would have made that call look 2.7x better than it was
topNews.actionable: New standing rule for this pipeline: only trust a published percent-change when the quoted previous close matches the known prior settle; otherwise compute the delta manually. This is the second time a self-flattering number nearly reached your dashboard.

topNews.headline: Iran hardens further: six published conditions for reopening, and "no possibility of resuming negotiations"
topNews.actionable: This is why crude did not gap dollars: a reopening was never actually imminent, so there was less mispricing to correct than we implied. It also means the Gulf risk premium is structural for now, not a headline spike.

topNews.headline: Houthis claim a drone strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery; Saudi confirms the fire was extinguished, no casualties
topNews.actionable: The conflict is widening beyond the strait to Saudi production infrastructure. Combined with traffic down a third, this is a slow supply squeeze rather than a single event — supportive for energy and, indirectly, for the metals bid.

topNews.headline: WEDNESDAY IS THE WEEK: US July CPI and Tencent Q2 results land on the same day
topNews.actionable: Two of your largest exposures resolve on one day — the levered silver leg via CPI, and your single biggest HK holding via Tencent. With SGX shut today, you have Tuesday alone to position the Singapore sleeve beforehand.

topNews.headline: Metals barely reacted: gold futures literally unchanged, silver +0.70%
topNews.actionable: After a 20%+ week in GDX, the weekend escalation produced no follow-through and no give-back. On 1.6x leverage a +0.70% silver move is ~+1.1% on the position — immaterial. The complex is waiting for CPI, which is the real driver here, not Hormuz.

signals: Brent losing Friday's $83.55 settle during Asian hours would mean the weekend escalation has fully round-tripped — that is the level to watch, not the headline.
The metals are no longer trading the Gulf; they are trading the Fed. A hot CPI Wednesday is the single biggest threat to the 1.6x levered silver leg, which has run from ~$55.6 to ~$63.9.
Tencent results Wednesday put your largest HK holding in play on the same day as CPI — an unusually concentrated risk day for this book.
SGX shut today compresses the Singapore decision window to Tuesday alone, right after record DBS and OCBC results with the STI 15 points off its high.
Crypto has now failed to join the metals rally two weekends running — the debasement trade is not moving as one.
